messages:
Lena: running a short triage from the prefix shadow-repair spike. goal: pick a production-safe protocol for repairing stale prefix reads without blowing up rehydrate traffic. notes below.
Omar: tl;dr of options?
Lena: three we prototyped:
  1) sync-verify: block read until owner responds, fall back if mismatch
  2) async-verify + eager repair: return fast, then immediately rehydrate on mismatch
  3) async-verify + deferred repair queue: return fast, enqueue for rate-limited rehydrate work
Priya: tradeoffs: 1 is correct but adds tail latency for everyone. 2 is aggressive and risks thundering. 3 seems safest but introduces repair lag window — might surface stale reads for a short time.
Ben: are we measuring how often deferred repairs are actually needed? i.e., mismatch rates broken down by cause: pre-handoff vs write-lag vs compaction timing?
Lena: spike numbers: overall mismatch 0.04% sampled, of those: 60% due to handoff race, 30% RW lag, 10% compaction/tombstone reorder.
Omar: so handoff races are the big target — can we fold in a short-lived soft-lease during handoff to reduce mismatch rather than repair?
Priya: we discussed soft-lease in RFC but it complicates demote path. still worth adding as preventative. combination approach: short soft-lease + deferred repairs for residuals.
Lena: proposed protocol (hybrid):
  - sample_rate: 2% shadow reads for the first rollout
  - verification: async sampling
  - handoff-detect: if owner responds with handoff flag -> trigger priority fast rehydrate (but capped)
  - mismatch handling: if mismatch and not handoff -> enqueue deferred repair with per-prefix cooldown
  - safety caps: global_rehydrate_qps = 100, per_tenant_rehydrate_qps = 2, per_prefix_cooldown = 30s
Priya: per-prefix cooldown important to avoid loops on hot prefixes. also add token-bucket window so bursts are smoothed.
Ben: we should avoid doing full payload diffs on every shadow. add a cheap precheck header (prefix-seq or checksum) and only diff payload when it differs. cheap precheck reduces CPU.
Lena: implemented prefix-seq header in spike. payload diffs dropped ~65%.
Omar: eviction interaction: if a prefix is demoted and later rehydrated frequently, we risk oscillation. how do we coordinate repair with eviction policy?
Priya: idea: when deferred repair enqueues, bump prefix eviction score temporarily (penalize for rehydrate) so it stays resident until repair completes. that prevents immediate re-evict/re-rehydrate cycles. need metrics for "repair-in-flight" which act like soft pins.
Ben: what about correctness windows for read-after-write? some clients expect linearizable reads for short duration after writes. can we wire a cheap write token to readers to prefer owner reads for recent writes?
Lena: we can propagate a write-seq token to client-facing caches for a short TTL; readers with that token are routed to authoritative path. impacts routing logic but keeps consistency for RW flows.
Omar: rollout plan and gating?
Lena: rollout phases: internal debug -> 1% tenants -> 5% tenants -> opt-in alpha. gates: mismatch_rate_on_production_sample < 0.5%, rehydrate_qps < 0.2% of read_qps, repair-failure-rate < 1%.
Priya: alarms: excess rehydrate RPS, sustained queued repairs > X, per-prefix repair loop detection. runbook items: 1) flip sample_rate to 0, 2) pause rehydrate workers, 3) manual prefix quarantine + rehydrate backfill. I'll draft runbook.
Ben: please add telemetry: cause-tagged mismatch (handoff, rw-lag, compaction), repair_latency_histogram, repair_outcome(success/fail).
ci-bot: CI: shadow-repair unit tests passed. integration smoke on staging scheduled for 2025-04-10T09:00Z.
Lena: next actions: Priya writes runbook, Omar builds soft-lease fallback RFC addendum, Ben wires telemetry, I'll land the deferred-queue + cooldown POC. aim to start internal debug next week. Any objections?
Omar: no objections.:+1:
Priya: on it.
Ben: will add dashboards to the "prefix-cache" board.
Lena: thanks team. I'll follow-up with a short RFC note and the sample configs.
